subject: Trial accountability & SLA/KPI commitments for LumenGuard POC
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@lumenguard.com>
Cc: Natal ie Chen <natalie.chen@lumenguard.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps after today’s demo

Alex / Natalie — thanks for the time earlier. Good alignment on the core evaluation goals. Per our call, I wanted to capture the proposed POC scope, success metrics, and owners so we have a single reference. Please reply with anything I missed.

High-level objective:
- Validate that Redwood inference can meet LumenGuard’s real-time summarization and alert enrichment workflow at target SLAs and unit cost.

Proposed POC (3 weeks):
1) Week 0 (prep): exchange sample traces, network diagram, and security checklist (RG NDA scope).
2) Week 1 (integration + baseline): run sample workload, measure baseline latency, throughput, token counts.
3) Week 2 (optimization): enable batching, prefix caching, and recommended quantization profile; iterate.
4) Week 3 (readout): produce final scorecard and handoff doc.

Success KPIs (draft):
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 180ms for 512 token requests (when routed to hosted cluster in us-west).
- Throughput: sustained 45 req/s for steady-state batch windows while maintaining latency target.
- Cost: average effective cost <= $0.004/token after batching and KV caching.
- Quality: summary fidelity (ROUGE-L or human sampling) comparable to current baseline; targeted F1 >= 0.80 on the labeled validation set we shared.

Ownership:
- Redwood: ben_carter (commercial lead), priyom_das (solutions engineer), marissa_cole (CS lead).
- LumenGuard: Alex (technical lead), Natalie (product owner), Security group for checklist.

Attachments: I uploaded a draft trial plan and network diagram (attached).

Next steps (please confirm by EOD Tuesday):
- LumenGuard to confirm sample dataset delivery and internal owners.
- Security team to scan the attached checklist; we can run the private endpoint if needed.
- Redwood to schedule integration slot (60–90 minutes) for Week 1.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@lumenguard.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@lumenguard.com>, security@lumenguard.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps after today’s demo

Thanks Ben — this is a helpful summary. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Timeline: can we stretch to 4 weeks? We have a compliance window and want an extra week for internal QA and edge-case labeling.
- Latency target: our current internal SLA is 150ms p95 for <400 token requests; is the 180ms target tied to 512 tokens only? We may need two buckets (short vs long).
- Data delivery: we will provide 3 example weekend traces and the validation label set by Thursday.

Security note (cc’d): our security team will run the checklist and flag any requirements for a private deployment — we’ll aim to get that back by Friday.

Also looping in our infra engineer, Mike (mike.leung@lumenguard.com), who will coordinate the network NAT and peering for the private endpoint if needed.

—Alex
VP Product, LumenGuard
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@lumenguard.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@lumenguard.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Quick recap + next steps after today’s demo

Appreciate the quick reply, Alex. Two quick technical clarifications and a refined KPI proposal so the test matrix is actionable: 

1) Latency buckets: we’ll measure p95 for two payload classes — short (<= 400 tokens) and long (401–800 tokens). Proposed targets: short p95 <= 150ms; long p95 <= 220ms. We’ll report both.

2) Throughput expectations: to simulate production, please indicate peak concurrency (typical bursts/minute). For planning assume 60 req/s sustained (we’ll throttle to 45 if you want a conservative run).

3) Cost accounting: we’ll produce two cost numbers — raw per-token and effective cost after batching/caching; example: raw $0.006/token -> effective $0.0035/token after batching. We’ll include a simple cost model in the readout.

4) Quality: in addition to automated ROUGE-L, we’ll run a 50-sample blind human evaluation for edge cases (privacy redaction, hallucination rate). Define acceptable thresholds now: max hallucination rate 5% on the sample set; avg human rating >= 3.8/5.

Action items I’ll take:
- Share a tailored runbook with command samples and the quantization profile we recommend (attachment: LumenGuard_trial_plan_v1.pdf).
- Book an integration window for Week 1 (60–90m).

If LumenGuard prefers a 4-week calendar, we’re fine — call that the standard POC+QA. Confirm and we’ll update dates.

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
From: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@lumenguard.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@lumenguard.com>, security@lumenguard.com, mike.leung@lumenguard.com
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 08:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps after today’s demo

Thanks Priyom — the bucketed latency targets are perfect and the dual-cost reporting is exactly what we need for procurement. We’d like one small addition to the scorecard: error-rate monitoring (5xx and timeouts) with alerting thresholds (5xx <= 0.5% monthly during the test).

We confirm the extended 4-week plan so we can run internal QA in Week 4. Tentative calendar (please update if it conflicts):
- Week 0 (setup): 22–24 Nov: data and checklist exchange.
- Week 1 (integration): 29 Nov–3 Dec: baseline runs and smoke tests.
- Week 2 (optimization): 6–10 Dec: batching, caching, model params.
- Week 3 (readout + QA): 13–17 Dec: internal QA, human eval, final readout.

We will deliver sample traces by Thu 18 Nov and the labeled validation set by Fri 19 Nov. Security will respond separately; Mike will coordinate network specifics.

Natalie
Product Manager, LumenGuard
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@lumenguard.com>, Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@lumenguard.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, security@lumenguard.com
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps after today’s demo

Great — thanks for the fast confirmations. I’ve updated the attached trial plan to reflect the 4-week cadence, bucketed latency SLAs, error-rate alerting threshold, and the readout cost model. Please see LumenGuard_trial_plan_v1.pdf (v1.1) attached in Drive; I also pasted the short scorecard we’ll deliver at the end of the POC below.

End-of-POC scorecard (deliverable):
- Latency (p95): short <= 150ms; long <= 220ms
- Throughput: 45 req/s sustained with documented burst behavior to 60 req/s
- Cost: effective cost <= $0.0038/token (after batching/caching)
- Quality: human eval >= 3.8/5 and hallucination rate <= 5%
- Error rate: 5xx/timeouts <= 0.5% during test runs

Immediate next steps:
- LumenGuard: deliver traces + labels by 19 Nov (per Natalie).
- Security: provide checklist feedback by Fri 19 Nov.
- Redwood: we’ll send calendar invites for Week 1 integration and share the runbook.

If we’re aligned I’ll convert this thread into a HubSpot milestone and circulate a master calendar invite.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
